answer.rationale: The two measured declines are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and the inherited record points at onboarding/activation work (memory_86, memory_31, memory_91) as the lever that moves exactly those metrics. Competitor entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the emotionally obvious answer, but memory_73 is precisely the memory that should not be trusted at face value for a 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective: it reports a 12-week window in a low-touch segment with the support model held constant, so it evidences a short-horizon conversion/revenue bump and says nothing about renewal-cycle retention, discount-cohort quality, margin, or price-anchoring damage. Matching a competitor on price also risks recruiting exactly the price-sensitive accounts that churn, which would degrade qualified revenue while flattering this quarter's numbers. So I spend one verification pull on memory_73 to see whether the archived record contains any post-window retention or cohort-quality data — if it does not, promotional_pricing is disqualified for this objective rather than merely deprioritized. I spend the second pull on memory_86, the memory my intended action leans on hardest, to check whether the 'improved completion and time-to-value' finding was measured on the same self-serve population now declining, and whether 'lifted early product adoption' was ever traced through to retained revenue or stops at an early funnel proxy. Verifying the memory I intend to act on, not just the one I intend to reject, is the point. Caveats I am carrying forward rather than resolving: memory_31 is day 12 and calls its lift 'durable' on a very short base, so I treat it as weak corroboration only; the current declines may stem from a product or mix change rather than onboarding length, in which case shortening onboarding will not recover them; and cutting signup friction can remove self-qualification, raising activation counts while lowering account quality. Therefore I run a standard experiment, not a broad rollout, holdout-controlled, with success judged on qualified-account and retained-revenue guardrails rather than completion or activation alone — the same downstream measurement memory_73 lacks. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) and referral_incentive (memory_57) address segments that are not where the decline is; they remain live candidates for the next slot.
